analysis: The PR changes two test-only stub classes. In EngineV2LivenessRecoveryTests.swift (line 124, LivenessStubLanguageModel) and EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift (line 158, WiringStubLanguageModel), the LanguageModel.prepare signature moves from (cache:, windowSize:) to (cache:, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters). This tracks an upstream mlx-swift-lm protocol change. Both stub bodies are unchanged (.tokens(input.text)), and they are never forward-passed. Both are in the Tests directory and ship in no production binary. Head and base are otherwise identical in the liveness test file (diffed visually; only line 124 differs). The changes touch no production code paths: no attestation, no coordinator WebSocket, no key handling, no prefix-cache or SSD storage (T-041), no fan helper and no App Attest authorization. No threat-model assumption is invalidated. One open integration question: the upstream dependency bump that causes this signature change (likely Package.swift/Package.resolved or a production LanguageModel conformance) is outside this batch. It should be reviewed separately for supply-chain and inference-engine behavior (TB-007, T-013). The new prepare parameters (state, prefill) could change prefill chunking and memory behavior in production, so a reviewer should confirm that production engine code adopting them preserves KV grant and budget invariants. This batch does not show that, and it is not a finding here.
